## 1. Open the Library and look at the shelf forge did not write

Four of the Library’s shelves hold parts forge ships.

![Open the Library and look at the shelf forge did not write](/media/stories/S8/01-open-the-library-and-look-at-the-shelf-f.png)

## 2. Press "Browse community"

One browser over four kinds — skills, hooks, MCPs and tools.

![Press "Browse community"](/media/stories/S8/02-press-browse-community.png)

## 3. Read where the twenty items actually come from

Nine sources are declared and four of them contribute nothing.

![Read where the twenty items actually come from](/media/stories/S8/03-read-where-the-twenty-items-actually-com.png)

## 4. Refresh the registry against those sources

forge crawls nothing on its own — a refresh happens exactly when an operator asks for one, and this is the ask.

![Refresh the registry against those sources](/media/stories/S8/04-refresh-the-registry-against-those-sourc.png)

## 5. Check what every declared source contributes — and what the ones contributing nothing say

This is what "browse the registry" has to mean, and it has three honest endings rather than one.

![Check what every declared source contributes — and what the ones contributing nothing say](/media/stories/S8/05-check-what-every-declared-source-contrib.png)

## 6. Read the rows the refresh wrote into the registry

A refresh does not only report what the sources publish — it writes it.

![Read the rows the refresh wrote into the registry](/media/stories/S8/06-read-the-rows-the-refresh-wrote-into-the.png)

## 7. Check the source forge could read and still had nothing to offer

The third ending, on its own chip.

![Check the source forge could read and still had nothing to offer](/media/stories/S8/07-check-the-source-forge-could-read-and-st.png)

## 8. Check that no row is still a hand-curated seed

Every row currently reads "seed — never verified", which is the truth and is exactly the problem.

![Check that no row is still a hand-curated seed](/media/stories/S8/08-check-that-no-row-is-still-a-hand-curate.png)

## 9. Take the first door in — press "+ Add item" to install by URL

The registry is a declared list, and this is how the operator declares something into it.

![Take the first door in — press "+ Add item" to install by URL](/media/stories/S8/09-take-the-first-door-in-press-add-item-to.png)

## 10. Give forge nothing but the upstream URL and what to call it

Star counts and last-checked dates are not on this form on purpose — they are facts a fetch establishes, not claims an operator types.

![Give forge nothing but the upstream URL and what to call it](/media/stories/S8/10-give-forge-nothing-but-the-upstream-url-.png)

## 11. Install the thing that URL names

This is §3’s second door, and it was a wall until ruling 477 built it.

![Install the thing that URL names](/media/stories/S8/11-install-the-thing-that-url-names.png)

## 12. Go back to the browser

Back to the catalogue, to take the door that does end in an install.

![Go back to the browser](/media/stories/S8/12-go-back-to-the-browser.png)

## 13. Find the one item in the registry that is executable code

Twenty items and exactly one of them is a script.

![Find the one item in the registry that is executable code](/media/stories/S8/13-find-the-one-item-in-the-registry-that-i.png)

## 14. Open it and read every file in the package before trusting any of it

Two files: the manifest that declares what it runs on and what it may touch, and the script itself.

![Open it and read every file in the package before trusting any of it](/media/stories/S8/14-open-it-and-read-every-file-in-the-packa.png)

## 15. Read the security scan that runs before the install exists

The order is the whole point: scanned before installed, not installed then scanned.

![Read the security scan that runs before the install exists](/media/stories/S8/15-read-the-security-scan-that-runs-before-.png)

## 16. Take the second door in — install it by id

Installed, and trusted by nobody.

![Take the second door in — install it by id](/media/stories/S8/16-take-the-second-door-in-install-it-by-id.png)

## 17. Follow it to the page that owns the trust decision

A hook that came from a stranger arrives in the same state as one the operator wrote by hand: on disk, described, scanned, and refused permission to run.

![Follow it to the page that owns the trust decision](/media/stories/S8/17-follow-it-to-the-page-that-owns-the-trus.png)

## 18. Approve it

One press, and a file somebody else wrote becomes something forge will execute.

![Approve it](/media/stories/S8/18-approve-it.png)

## 19. Open the Agents pillar

A library part is inert until something composes it.

![Open the Agents pillar](/media/stories/S8/19-open-the-agents-pillar.png)

## 20. Find the installed hook in the palette an agent composes from

This is where S8 ends and where a community install becomes real: not when the bytes land, and not when the operator approves them, but when the thing shows up in the bin an agent is built out of.

![Find the installed hook in the palette an agent composes from](/media/stories/S8/20-find-the-installed-hook-in-the-palette-a.png)
